items.body:
sunflower tape machine Rebels Against Dream Pop Polish With Grit On 'I LIKE NOISE. MATTER OF FACT, I LOVE IT.'

9 September 2026

After some breakout singles earlier this decade that steadily led him to play the main stage at Lollapalooza India 2026, Aryaman Singh aka sunflower tape machine, has finally released his debut album, 'I LIKE NOISE. MATTER OF FACT, I LOVE IT.'

While his earlier work featured chiming synths and guitars, and reverb-drenched vocals to give his saccharine melodies a dreampop quality, the new 8-track release sees the Chennai artist abandon it to embrace a love for noise, proclaiming it in the title itself.

"I think we as an industry take noise for granted. For the longest time, my art ended up sounding so sterile and insincere because I’d try to abide by “industry standards," says Aryaman. That doesn't mean the album fully changes genre. There is one puristic noise work with 'A LOVE LETTER TO NOISE', an interlude in the 8-track run, and an outright rejection of expectations with tracks like 'I DON'T WANT TO WRITE ANOTHER LOVE SONG', but the singer-songwriter's penchant for upbeat melodies continues to take centre stage.

It just now comes backed by guitars that are distorting into walls of sizzling energy rather than shimmering like they used to, and even the still-present backbeat is crushed under its own energy. It's a befitting musical backing for the themes of angst, conflict and the gusto to rise above that the lyrics deal with. The result might alienate a good few cursory fans who preferred the easier palette of sunflower tape machine's earlier work, but those who stay will find something that is undoubtedly deeper, more authentic and teeming with energy.

Listen to 'I LIKE NOISE. MATTER OF FACT, I LOVE IT.' below and head to sunflower tape machine's artist profile for more information.

items.body:
Hopeful Melodies Pair With Grief & Anxiety-Inspired Lyrics On Lotus Flower's 'A Night of the Jumps'

8 September 2026

When he chose the moniker 'Lotus Flower' for himself, it was clear Shriraj Sagara wasn't trying to hide that he is influenced by Radiohead, his voice often choosing the relaxed, high-pitched falsetto singing that has defined frontman Thom Yorke's work. The Ahmedabad-rooted, Berlin-based musician continues to gradually build upon that influence in his latest EP 'A Night of the Jumps'.

The melodies of the falsetto singing lend more to the atmosphere of synth arpeggios, horn lines and steady percussion rather than inviting the limelight. Meanwhile, Shriraj's compositions carry a more uplifting quality even as they deal with an unsettled mixture of anxiety, grief and vulnerability. Notably, the pounding rhythm section of opener 'Ceremony', unlike the formerly mentioned namesake influence, keeps things more communal and inviting than introspective, even as the song attempts to capture the coldness and disorientation of a difficult winter.

The subtly gritty and detuned synth foundations of 'A Small Town Cries' harken more to the nostalgia found in works by acts like Boards of Canada, though the lyrics draw from fragments of news from Israel's war on Gaza. The track Shriraj join hands again with his brother Shantanu Sagara for another DIY music video, though with less production value than their previous stellar work 'Wilting'.

Check out 'A Night of the Jumps' below and follow Shriraj Sagara on Instagram for more information.
